title: New-Home Courtesy for HomeFlood Customers Moving to NFIP Coverage
content:
**Rule.** A customer closing out a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy who has insured a new primary residence with Tidemark's federal book receives a new-home courtesy. That book is the NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own).

**The qualifying policy.** The customer must hold a Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy that:
- is in force (status in force);
- is on the customer's primary residence;
- is at an address different from the HomeFlood property address.

**The courtesy.** It depends on how far that NFIP policy's original effective date lies from the request's effective date. The distance is counted in calendar days in either direction.

| NFIP policy's original effective date, from the request's effective date | New-home courtesy |
|---|---|
| no more than 60 days | 25 USD |
| more than 60 but no more than 180 days | 10 USD |
| more than 180 days, or no such NFIP policy | none |

**Form of the courtesy.** The courtesy is an amount taken off the closing payment.

**Records read.** The NFIP Dwelling Form policy record is read for its status, its primary-residence designation, its property address and its original effective date.

**The request on file.** The request on file is the policy's signed cancellation request — the latest received when more than one is signed, and the one recorded first among requests received on the same date; a withdrawn or unsigned request never counts — read for its reason, its effective date and its supporting document.

## Hypothetical cases (request effective 1 September)

| NFIP primary-residence policy in force at another address, original effective date | Courtesy |
|---|---|
| 15 August | 25.00 (17 days) |
| 30 October | 25.00 (59 days) |
| 1 May | 10.00 (123 days) |
| a second home in force at another address, not the primary residence | none |
